conversation to it.
# dsh-turn-clock
English | 中文
A right-sidebar tab for DeepSeek Harness that lists **every turn of the current session with the dat
e and time it started**, and jumps the conversation to the turn you click.
Prompt text is mosaicked so a real conversation stays private; the dates, times and layout are unedi
pt text is mosaicked so a real conversation stays private; the dates, times and layout are unedited.
## Why
DSH already has a turn rail on the right edge of the conversation, and it is good: it lists turns, p
reviews them, and jumps. Two things it does not do:
- **It carries no time.** The `turnOutline` projection it renders has only `turn / seq / prompt / re

sponse`, so there is nothing to date a turn with.
- **It disappears when the transcript is narrow.**
The rail is not rendered at all when the transcript's available width is ≤ 900 px — which is exactl
y when you open a sidebar.
This plugin is the second surface for the same question: a real page in the right Sidebar, grouped b
y calendar day, one row per turn, each row showing `HH:mm` plus the start of that turn's prompt. Cli
ck a row to go there.
## How this compares
Turn navigation is a crowded corner of the DSH plugin ecosystem. Being precise about what differs is
more useful than claiming novelty:
| | Surface | Dates/times | Depends on |
| **dsh-turn-clock** (this) | A tab in the **official right Sidebar** | Per-turn date + `HH:mm`, gro

uped by day, from the whole log | Nothing beyond DSH itself |
| Built-in turn rail | Strip on the co

nversation's right edge | None | — (but hidden when the transcript is ≤ 900 px wide) |
| dsh-convers

ation-timeline | Horizontal dock above the composer | Turn start time on each capsule | Nothing |
|
dsh-turn-outline | Right-sidebar tab | None (folds input + tool steps + output) | Peer `dsh-better-s

idebar` |
| dsh-timeline | Axis on the conversation's right edge | None advertised | Nothing (much l
arger: pins, favourites, prompt library, export) |
The one-line version: **a dated outline in the official right sidebar, with no other plugin required
one-line version: **a dated outline in the official right sidebar, with no other plugin required.**
## Features
| Feature | Detail |

| Dated outline | One row per turn, grouped under `11月2日 周日`-style day headers, newest last |
| Clic
k to jump | Pages history in through the turn's `turn/start` seq, then scrolls the turn's transcript

row into view |
| Whole-log coverage | Times come from a Host projection folded over the **entire**

session log, so turns the browser never loaded are still listed |
| Keyboard | Rows are focusable;

`Enter` and `Space` jump |
| Locale | Chinese and English copy, following the app locale |
| No othe
r plugin needed | Uses the official right Sidebar — no `dsh-better-sidebar` peer |
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then restart DSH (or refresh the page). From a local checkout:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Built and tested against DSH `0.2.1-rc.5`. The plugin uses documented extension seams plus two inter
nal contracts listed below, so a future DSH release can break the jump (see *What this depends on*).
## Use
Open the right Sidebar → **Start (指南 / Guide)** → the **Turn timeline (时间目录)** card. The first turn
of a session is the top row; the list opens scrolled to the newest turn.
Where it lives: the guide's card list, one card among the shipped tools.
## How it works
**Host half** (index.js) registers one `turnClock` projection unit on `ctx.sessionProjections`:

- `turn/start` appends `{ turn, t: event.time, s: event.seq, p: '' }`
- the first human `user/messag
e` of that turn fills `p` with a 120-character preview (injected context and tool results are exclud

ed by checking `source.kind === 'user'`)
- `wire.view` returns the state object itself, so an unchan
ged fold publishes nothing
**Client half** (client.js):
- registers a tab type through `ctx.sidebarRightTabs.register()` and its body under the keyed `sideb

ar.right.pane.tab` slot, plus a guide entry
- reads the projection with the standard `useProjection(

'turnClock')` keyed hook
- jumps with `ctx.sessions.binding(sessionId).session.loadThrough(seq)`, th
en `scrollIntoView` on the transcript row
## What this depends on
This is a third-party plugin, not a first-party seam. Two internals are load-bearing, and both are n
amed here on purpose:
1. **`data-chat-turn="<n>"`** — Chat puts the turn number on every transcript row. The jump finds it

s target with this attribute. Chat uses the same attribute for its own reading-position tracking.
2.
**`binding.session.loadThrough(seq)`** — the jump loader Chat's own rail calls when a turn is not l
oaded yet. Accessed through `ctx.sessions.binding(sessionId)`.
If either changes upstream:
- **Times and the list keep working** — they only depend on the projection seam and the slot system.
- **The jump degrades gracefully** — the panel shows a one-line reason at its foot instead of throw
*The jump degrades gracefully** — the panel shows a one-line reason at its foot instead of throwing.
A `turnOutline` projection is read as a fallback source of per-turn seqs, so a jump still works when
this package's own projection predates a field.
## Known limitations
- **Turns removed by compaction cannot be jumped to.** Once a turn is no longer part of the session
surface it has no row in the DOM; the row stays listed (the projection still knows it started) but c

licking it reports that it could not be found. The built-in rail has the same limit.
- **Centered, n

ot top-aligned.** The jump centers the turn; Chat's own rail aligns it 24 px below the top edge.
- *
*No view switching.** If you are in the Trajectory view rather than Chat, there are no transcript ro

ws to scroll; the panel says so instead of switching views for you.
- **Day labels follow the browse

r locale** via `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, which is usually but not always the app locale.
- **Timestamps
are turn starts.** The time is the `turn/start` event, i.e. the moment the loop began the turn righ
t after your prompt — not when a message first painted.
